title: An Information-Theoretic Characterization of Optimal Value-Readout in Response-Register Quantum Oracles
authors: Milad Ghadimi, Hesam Soltanpanahi, Vahid Salari
abstract: Response-register quantum oracles admit two complementary operational interpretations: value readout and phase kickback. Although their computational equivalence is well understood, the quantitative relation between these two operational interpretations has lacked an exact characterization. We prove that, for finite Abelian response groups, the optimal single-query value-readout probability is exactly the normalized Rényi-1/2 effective Fourier support of the response state. This identity provides an exact information-theoretic characterization of optimal value-readout capability, gives the Rényi-1/2 effective Fourier support a direct operational interpretation in the oracle setting, and yields a tight phase--value complementarity theorem together with an explicit family of saturating response states.
summary: This work characterizes optimal value readout in response-register quantum oracles by proving that the achievable probability is exactly determined by the normalized Rényi-1/2 effective Fourier support of the state. This establishes an exact information-theoretic measure, providing a tight complementarity theorem between phase and value measurements for Abelian groups.
main_problem: The paper aims to provide an exact, quantitative characterization of the relationship between two complementary operational interpretations—value readout and phase kickback—for response-register quantum oracles.
main_result: It proves that for finite Abelian response groups, the optimal single-query value-readout probability is exactly equal to the normalized Rényi-1/2 effective Fourier support of the response state.
method: The analysis uses information theory, linking optimal quantum state discrimination (covariant measurements) to properties derived from the Fourier-weight distribution of the response state via group theory concepts.
model_or_system: The model is a response-register quantum oracle acting on a computational register and characterized by a finite Abelian response group $A$. The system's behavior is governed by the response state $|\etaangle$ and its associated Fourier-weight distribution $p = (p_\chi)$.
key_observables: Optimal single-query value-readout probability ($P_{	ext{val}}$), Rényi-1/2 effective Fourier support ($	ext{Seff}$), and target character phase fidelity ($\Phi$).
important_parameters: The dimension of the response register, $d = |A|$, and the specific structure of the Abelian group $A$.
main_assumptions: The results are rigorously proven only for finite Abelian response groups; extensions to non-Abelian groups are suggested as future work.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the oracle's two interpretations (value readout vs. phase kickback), map out the achievable phase–value tradeoff region, and show the 'Effective Fourier-support landscape' relating $P_{	ext{val}}$ to the distribution $p$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes a chain of correspondences: linking the operational limit ($P_{	ext{val}}$) through quantum state discrimination theory to an information-theoretic quantity ($	ext{Seff}$), which is defined via the R\'enyi-1/2 entropy of the Fourier weights.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical connection between geometric properties (Fourier support) and operational limits ($P_{	ext{val}}$) provides a powerful, generalizable tool for analyzing quantum measurement protocols in structured settings.
